\frac14\le a\le\frac12,\; \frac14\le d\le\frac12 .
\]

Substituting in (2) gives a function of the two variables \(a,d\):

\[
\boxed{%
P(a,d)=
(2a-\tfrac12)(a+\tfrac12-d)(a+d)(1-a-d)
\bigl(\tfrac12+d-a\bigr)(2d-\tfrac12) } .
\tag{3}
\]

Both factors in (3) are symmetric in \(a\) and \(d\); the feasible region is
the square \([\,\tfrac14,\tfrac12\,]^2\) with the additional condition
\(a+d<1\) (otherwise the factor \(1-a-d\) would vanish).

--------------------------------------------------------------------

### 4.  Symmetry forces \(a=d\)

The function \(P(a,d)\) is symmetric: \(P(a,d)=P(d,a)\).
If an interior maximum exists, the gradient must be zero.
Because of the symmetry the only interior critical point must satisfy  

\[
a=d .
\tag{4}
\]

(If the maximum lay on a side of the square, at least one factor in (3) would
be zero, giving product \(0\); hence the maximum cannot be on the boundary.)

--------------------------------------------------------------------

### 5.  One‑variable maximisation  

Put \(a=d=t\;( \tfrac14<t<\tfrac12)\).  
Then \(b=c=\frac12-t\) and (3) reduces to  

\[
P(t)=\bigl(2t-\tfrac12\bigr)^2\;t\;(1-2t)\;\Bigl(\tfrac12\Bigr)^2
= \frac14\,(2t-\tfrac12)^2\,t\,(1-2t) .
\]

Let \(u=2t\in[\tfrac12,1]\); then

\[
P(u)=\frac14\,(u-\tfrac12)^2\,u\,(1-u).
\]

Differentiating,

\[
\frac{d}{du}\Big[(u-\tfrac12)^2 u (1-u)\Big]
  =-4u^{3}+6u^{2}-\frac52u+\frac14=0,
\]

which gives, in the interval \([\tfrac12,1]\),

\[
u=\frac12+\frac{\sqrt2}{4}.
\]

Consequently  

\[
t=\frac{u}{2}= \frac{2+\sqrt2}{8},\qquad
b=c=\frac{2-\sqrt2}{8}.
\]

Substituting these values into \(P(t)\),

\[
P_{\max}= \frac14\,
\Bigl(\frac{\sqrt2}{4}\Bigr)^{\!2}
\cdot\frac{2+\sqrt2}{8}\cdot\Bigl(1-\frac{2+\sqrt2}{4}\Bigr)
= \frac{1}{256}.
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------

### 6.  Attaining the maximum  

Thus the maximum is attained for

\[
\boxed{\;
x_{1}= -\frac{2+\sqrt2}{8},\;
x_{2}= -\frac{2-\sqrt2}{8},\;
x_{3}= \frac{2-\sqrt2}{8},\;
x_{4}= \frac{2+\sqrt2}{8}
\;}
\]

(which indeed satisfy \(x_{1}+x_{2}+x_{3}+x_{4}=0\) and
\(|x_{1}|+|x_{2}|+|x_{3}|+|x_{4}|=1\)).

For this 4‑tuple  

\[
\prod_{1\le i<j\le4}(x_i-x_j)=\frac{1}{256},
\]

and any other admissible 4‑tuple gives a smaller value.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
\[
\boxed{\displaystyle \max \prod_{1\le i<j\le4}(x_i-x_j)=\frac{1}{256}}
